result.summary: Design validation for PLC-01..04 failed: 3 BLOCKER open questions unresolved (OQ-2, OQ-1, OQ-3), 4 MAJOR gaps in acceptance-criterion coverage.

issues.description: Open question PLC-01 OQ-2 unresolved: module_id scope - globally unique or per-tenant? The design primary key is (module_id, version) but module_id repetition across tenants would make module_id alone non-unique globally. This affects the share-table join condition in PLC-04 resolveModuleRef and the grant uniqueness semantics. Confirm the scope before BACKEND-DEV implements.

Open question PLC-03 OQ-1 unresolved: immediately preceding ACTIVE version - is it the highest semver below the new version (e.g. 2.0.1 for 3.0.0), or the highest within the same major? The design algorithm does ORDER BY semver_sort(version) DESC LIMIT 1 which selects the global highest below the new version. Confirm which interpretation is correct.

Open question PLC-04 OQ-3 unresolved: Should grantModuleVisibility and revokeModuleVisibility emit structured audit_log events? The design only says recommend yes with no firm decision. Audit log is an important NFR requirement for administrative actions in a multi-tenant system. ORCH or PRODUCT_OWNER must decide.

PLC-01 AC not covered: GIVEN both child_definition_id and module_ref are present on the same node, WHEN the definition is created or updated, THEN it is rejected with HTTP 422. The design never mentions this dual-presence validation. graph.zig existing checkSubProcess only validates child_definition_id is present - it would not catch this case. BACKEND-DEV needs explicit guidance to add this check.

PLC-01 error taxonomy gap: what happens when publishModule is called on a module version already in ACTIVE status? PLC-02 edge-case table mentions ModuleAlreadyActive but PLC-01 ModuleCatalogError enum does not include it and no HTTP response is specified. Implementor would not know whether to return 409, 422, or something else.

PLC-03 OQ-2: What if new version is the first ACTIVE (no predecessor)? The design says produces no warning (null) but the algorithm pseudocode always calls computeCompatibilityWarning(newEntry, previousEntry) assuming previousEntry exists. The null-handling case needs explicit description in the algorithm.

PLC-03 OQ-3: absent required defaults to false is stated as confirmed but the algorithm has a bug handling it. When prev.required is absent (null) it equals false so the check prev.required == false and input.required == true does not fire for the case where a previously-absent (optional) input is now required=true. The algorithm needs explicit null/absent handling: treat absent required as false at the point of comparison.
